title: Simpson’s Paradox & Aggregation Bias
interviewAnswer: A trend can reverse after stratifying by a confounding/grouping variable because aggregate weights differ. Always inspect important segments before interpreting an overall association.
keyPoints: Different group composition can reverse comparisons.
Causal conclusions need more than stratification alone.
why: Simpson’s Paradox & Aggregation Bias is a standard part of a broad data/ML curriculum because it changes how models are selected, evaluated or operated in real systems.
deepDive: A trend can reverse after stratifying by a confounding/grouping variable because aggregate weights differ. Always inspect important segments before interpreting an overall association. Different group composition can reverse comparisons. Causal conclusions need more than stratification alone. A strong answer connects the formal idea to validation, data requirements and failure modes instead of treating the method as a recipe.
workedExample: Treatment A wins overall because it is used more often on easy cases, but loses within both easy and hard cases.
commonMistakes: Choosing the technique without checking whether its assumptions match the problem.
Optimizing an offline metric without checking realistic validation slices or operational constraints.
followUps: When would you not use Simpson’s Paradox & Aggregation Bias?
How would you validate or tune Simpson’s Paradox & Aggregation Bias?
production: In production, validate on realistic slices, track latency/cost when relevant, and monitor for distribution changes or failure modes that the offline metric can hide.
